skills.name: Living and non-living; plants and animals

note.text:
Living things show all seven characteristics (MRS GREN); non-living things do not.
Differences between plants and animals:
• Plants make their own food by photosynthesis, using sunlight; animals eat food.
• Most plants are green: they contain chlorophyll. Animals have none.
• Plants stay in one place (they move only parts, slowly); most animals move from place to place.
• Plants grow all their lives; most animals stop growing when adult.
• Plant cells have a cell wall; animal cells do not.
• Animals respond quickly (nerves, muscles); plants respond slowly.

worked_example.problem: Give two ways in which a cassava plant is different from a goat.
steps: The cassava plant makes its own food using sunlight; the goat must eat food.
The cassava plant stays in one place; the goat moves from place to place.
worked_example.answer: It makes its own food, and it does not move from place to place.

cards.idea: Plants make their own food using sunlight (photosynthesis); animals must eat food.
example: A maize plant makes sugar in its green leaves; a goat eats the leaves.

cards.idea: Plants stay in one place and grow all their lives; most animals move about and stop growing when adult.
example: A tree keeps growing taller for many years.

cards.idea: Plant cells have a cell wall and chlorophyll; animal cells have neither.

check.prompt: Which is true of plants but not animals?

right.text: They make their own food using sunlight.
Their cells have a cell wall.

questions.prompt: Why do plants not need to move about to find food?

right.text: They make their own food using sunlight, water and carbon dioxide.

wrong.explain: All living things need food; plants make theirs.
They take water and minerals from the soil but make their food in the leaves.
Plants make their own food by photosynthesis.

right.text: Most animals move from place to place.
Plant cells have a cell wall.

Plants stop growing when they are a year old.
